Middle East.headline: Yemen — Hostilities Drive Mass Displacement and Escalating Disease Risks
Middle East.body: An estimated 125,000 people, including over 57,000 children, have been displaced in Yemen following escalated fighting since July between Houthi rebels, the Yemeni government, and Saudi Arabia. Rapid displacement has forced thousands to flee across the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Djibouti under extreme heat. Aid agencies and WHO warn that overcrowded conditions, combined with severe shortages of clean water and sanitation in Taiz, Lahj, and Aden, significantly heighten the risk of cholera, dengue fever, and malnutrition, while placing severe strain on a fragile healthcare system.

Middle East.headline: Iran — UN Mission Implicates US in Deadly Primary School Strike
Middle East.body: A UN fact-finding mission reported reasonable grounds to believe the United States conducted a February military strike on a primary school and sports facility in Minab, Hormozgan province, Iran. The attack, involving a Tomahawk missile that collapsed the roof of the clearly identifiable Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school, killed 156 civilians, including 120 children. The UN mission concluded that the strike constitutes a war crime.

Middle East.headline: Gaza Strip — Damaged Building Collapse Kills 21 Civilians
Middle East.body: A building collapse in the Gaza Strip killed 21 people who were sheltering inside, highlighting severe safety risks driven by acute housing shortages. The structure had been heavily damaged three years prior by an Israeli airstrike. The lack of viable shelter options across Gaza has forced displaced families to reside in structurally unstable and compromised buildings, posing severe protection hazards to civilians.

Americas.headline: Sexual and gender-based violence as a tool of criminal governance in Haiti
Americas.body: Posted on 18 Sep 2026 Women and girls are on the front line of Haiti’s security crisis. Across gang-controlled areas, the threat of rape, sexual exploitation and abuse by armed groups has become an everyday reality, making sexual and gender-based violence one of the most devastating consequences of the conflict. The erosion of state authority in Haiti has led to unprecedented levels of violence. Between 2024 and 2025, over 11 000 people were killed and more than 4 900 injured in gang conflicts. Africa.headline: Care Work Drives Deaths in Record Ebola Outbreak
Africa.body: Kinshasa, Geneva, 18 September 2026 - "I have just returned from Bunia, the epicentre of the Democratic Republic of the Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak - and what is now the fastest-growing outbreak on record. What I saw there was a bleak picture of what this outbreak does to women and girls. Women are on the front line - in health centres, in homes and in their communities. And they are paying the price, sometimes with their lives. Women and girls caring for the sick - young and old - as health workers in health centres, and as carers at home. Women and girls washing and burying the dead. Women and girls collecting water and food.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Airstrike Kills Three Family Members in Western Myanmar's Sagaing Region
Asia-Pacific.body: A Myanmar military regime airstrike killed three family members and injured four others in Sagaing Region’s Pale Township on Sept. 15, despite no active ground fighting in the area, according to residents and monitoring groups. Two junta gyrocopters deployed from the Northwestern Military Command dropped bombs twice on Kan Bauk (East) village, located about five miles from Pale town, at around noon. The victims—a mother, her son, and her daughter-in-law—were killed during one of the two bombing runs. Local sources confirmed that all three were cremated Wednesday evening. Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: DRC — Ebola Outbreak Kills Over 3,500 Across Seven Provinces
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its 17th Ebola outbreak, originating in Ituri province and expanding across seven northern and eastern provinces. More than 3,500 deaths have been recorded among over 7,200 cases. Despite a recent plateau in case numbers, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and Médecins Sans Frontières warned the outbreak remains out of control, with cases spreading into underprepared areas lacking basic response measures. Women and girls face disproportionate exposure and mortality due to their roles as primary caregivers in households and healthcare facilities, as well as during burial preparations.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Spain — Severe Flooding Causes Fatality and Disruption in East
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Slow-moving thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall, strong winds, and hail across eastern Spain, triggering severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia. At least one person died during the storms. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded over 100mm of rain in a few hours, including 70mm within 30 minutes in localized areas. The floodwaters submerged roads and vehicles and led to widespread flight cancellations.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: South Africa — Rapid Increase in Mpox Infections Concentrated in Western Cape
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: South Africa's Department of Health reported a rapid rise in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, reaching 18 confirmed infections and one probable case nationwide. The outbreak is concentrated primarily in Cape Town and the surrounding Western Cape province, which accounts for 15 of the confirmed cases. With support from the World Health Organization, health authorities secured limited supplies of the antiviral treatment Tecovirimat and called on the public to remain vigilant for symptoms.
